residual: P2: The de-fused exclusion sentence now follows the newly added write-back half and says "The rule does not apply to wave-raised escalations", so on a contract surface it reads as excluding wave-raised escalations from the escalation-answered write-back as well as from the escalation-opened append. Phase 2 step 7 (spec-loop.md:141-143) requires writing answers back for ALL open escalations, wave-raised included, and run_state.open_escalations() (run_state.py:1052-1076) holds any opened id open until an escalation-answered event with that id lands. The justification given ("already appended by persist-slice") only supports excluding the append, so the slice's own fix re-introduces a scope ambiguity of the kind it exists to remove.

P3: ANSWER_RE_ASK couples a doctrine pin to a Phase 2 step NUMBER. The number is correct today (spec-loop.md:137 is step 7 "Escalations"), but any future renumbering of Phase 2 breaks this test without the rule it guards having changed - the pin then fails for a reason unrelated to the doctrine, which trains readers to edit the pin rather than the prose.

P3: The implementer's deviation report states "lines 240-275 now report nothing over 93", but plan step 7's awk check still prints line 242 at 95 columns (the pre-existing osascript alert paragraph, untouched by this diff). The plan asked for anything printed in that range to be reported rather than reflowed; the report instead asserted a clean result. The edited lines themselves are all <= 93, so this is a reporting inaccuracy, not a code defect.
